Body:
I hit the same hang from a wrapper that leaves the child's stdin pipe open. #38723 now has a deterministic FIFO repro at run.ts:416, and the original reporter reproduced it and retracted the models.dev diagnosis.

I tested the alternative where a supplied positional message makes stdin ignored. It fixes the hang, but it also silently drops input from `opencode run "prompt" < file`, including the empty-positional cases. That mixed-input behavior was added explicitly, so I think `--no-stdin` is the safer interface.

I have subprocess tests that leave stdin open and fail by timeout on the current code, including empty positional and `-- ""` cases.

Cross-link from OpenChamber side: I'm running into exactly this on the OpenChamber fork. The current OPENCODE_CONFIG workaround doesn't work because OpenChamber spawns a single managed OpenCode process that serves multiple projects — they all share the env var, so a per-project config is impossible.

We have a workaround in OpenChamber fork PR #2917 ( ix/managed-opencode-health-timeout, MERGEABLE on the fork): the OpenChamber server now passes OPENCODE_CONFIG through to the managed OpenCode child process. But this only solves the *single-config-for-all-projects* case, not the per-project injection this issue is asking for.

A x-opencode-config header or config query param on the OpenCode HTTP API would unblock per-project injection. From the OpenChamber side this would mean:
- The OpenChamber client passes the project directory's resolved config (or a profile identifier) when calling OpenCode APIs
- The server reads it before resolving any config-derived state (providers, plugins, MCP, model defaults)
- No need to restart the managed server per project switch

Even a documented OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT env var (vs OPENCODE_CONFIG path) would help — OpenChamber could pass the resolved JSON inline without writing temp files.

Happy to test a PR against this if upstream wants to draft one. The OpenChamber-side plumbing is ready.

One thing worth noting in relation to the points already raised: the GUI implementation does work to some extent, but it is not actually doing a native skill invocation. It replaces the /<skill> invokation with the skill content into the prompt, which often causes the model to recognize and load the same skill again through its built-in skill discovery flow. In practice, this can result in the skill context being processed twice and increases token usage.

More importantly: Opencode's v2 beta already supports proper /<skill> invocation semantics. From my testing, it invokes the skill directly instead of treating the slash command as text that gets replaced by the skill contents first, so it avoids the double-loading behavior described above.

Worth noting the pricing gap specifically for gateway **`auto` router models** — e.g. `openrouter/auto`, `manifest/auto`, and Kilo Gateway's auto routes. These have no static per-token price in models.dev because the underlying model varies per request, so local catalog computation always resolves to $0.00 for them regardless of what rates are added.

The only source that can ever be correct for an `auto` route is the provider-reported `usage.cost` in the response. That reinforces the proposed `getUsage` change: prefer provider-reported cost when present (even `0` is meaningful for flat-fee subscription routes), and fall back to catalog rates otherwise.

Confirmed same class of bug in a **fresh session with NO plugins**, opencode 1.18.19, model `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash` (macOS ARM64). This rules out a plugin-triggered cause and suggests a general missing loop-detection issue.

Findings / observations:
1. **Triggers were not all identical in shape** — observed loops where the agent re-issued:
   - the same file `read` repeatedly,
   - the same `git add`/`git commit` repeatedly,
   - the same `git status` check repeatedly.
   In every case it re-emitted an identical tool call instead of executing once and moving on, with no self-correction until interrupted.
2. **It is intermittent, not deterministic** — a long multi-phase task (many sequential edits/commits/tests) progressed normally for a while, then entered a loop, then after interruption resumed normally.
3. **Mitigation that worked for us:** interrupting immediately (at the 2nd repeat) and issuing one explicit command per step (rather than letting it chain/repeat) let the work continue. Adding a hard rule "never repeat the same tool call twice; move on" to the session guidance also reduced occurrences.
4. **Impact:** each repetition consumes tokens; in a billing-metered session this caused significant token/billing swell and stalled progress.

Environment: opencode 1.18.19, deepseek-v4-flash, macOS 25.5.0 (Darwin ARM64/T6020), Node v26.5.0, no plugins.

Hope the loop/no-progress detection + circuit breaker (as referenced in #31942) lands soon.

Confirming this at production scale, and it's worse for multi-agent workflows than the log line suggests.

## Environment

- opencode version: 0.0.0-beta-17793
- OS: macOS (Darwin arm64)
- Terminal: tmux / xterm-256color
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: beta
- Active plugins: none configured

## Production evidence (single day, one machine)

From the server log (`Failed to drain Session` entries), all against `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions`:

- **116 ×** `AI.Error: RequestExecutor.read: Decode error (200 POST https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions)`
- **32 ×** `AI.Error: RequestExecutor.read: ECONNRESET: The socket connection was closed unexpectedly`

All of them fatal to the turn. Zero retried. The generic message is the *only* signal — there is no way to tell from the persisted error whether the provider truncated the body, sent malformed SSE, or the local socket died, which is exactly the diagnostic loss this issue describes.

## Why sub-agents make this acute

This machine runs a long-running multi-agent program (~90 sub-agent sessions/day through the Zen free models). For orchestrators, each one of these failures is a worker that dies silently:

- No terminal event reaches the parent session — from the coordinator's point of view the sub-agent is indistinguishable from "still working" or "stalled", so completion signals can't be trusted and the repo state has to be polled as ground truth.
- Whatever the dead turn had in flight is lost; re-dispatching means re-running the whole task from scratch, not resuming.
- Human operators fall back to manually nudging sessions with "continue" to kick a fresh request.

The failure rate scales with fleet size, so heavy sub-agent users absorb this superlinearly. Preserving the native cause + stream-progress metadata (as the PR does) would let tooling distinguish provider-side truncation from local transport faults and route retries accordingly — that distinction is exactly what's missing today.

Adding production data from a machine hitting this daily — with one wrinkle that may matter for the fix: even the error class this issue says *is* retryable (`ECONNRESET`) fails the session outright when it arrives wrapped by the AI SDK.

## Environment

- opencode version: 0.0.0-beta-17793
- OS: macOS (Darwin arm64)
- Terminal: tmux / xterm-256color
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: beta
- Active plugins: none configured

## What we see

Server log, single day, all against `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions`, all surfacing as `Failed to drain Session` and killing the turn:

```
AI.Error: RequestExecutor.read: ECONNRESET: The socket connection was closed unexpectedly. …   (32×)
AI.Error: RequestExecutor.read: Decode error (200 POST https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions)   (116×)
```

Session records show **no retry attempts** for any of these — the turn just ends. The `ECONNRESET` cases are notable because raw transport `ECONNRESET` is supposedly already in the retryable set; it's the `RequestExecutor.read:` wrapping (the same wrapping discussed in #42482) that appears to bypass classification. That matches the mechanism in #43791: errors that don't arrive as classifiable provider failures fall through to a terminal state.

## Request

For sub-agent orchestration this is the single most expensive failure mode: a coordinator dispatches N concurrent sub-agents, one stream dies mid-turn, no terminal event reaches the parent, and the coordinator can't distinguish "dead" from "stalled" — so the whole task gets re-run from scratch or a human manually nudges the session back to life.

Minimum viable behavior from our side:

1. Unwrap the AI SDK error chain (`cause` / `RequestExecutor.read` wrapper) before classification so mid-stream transport failures hit the existing retry policy (#43791 looks like the right place).
2. Cap the retries and surface a terminal state to clients when exhausted — currently failures are either silent-and-fatal (this issue) or silent-and-infinite (#21960), and both look identical from outside.

The root cause is in `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts` — the session loop exits on *any* finish reason that isn't `tool-calls`, so **any** model whose provider returns an empty `finish: unknown` / 0-token completion will trigger the silent stop. It is gateway/model-agnostic by construction.

Follow-up on v1.18.20 behavior change:

After updating to v1.18.20, the hard abort (UnknownError: terminated) is gone — but the new retry behavior introduced a different problem on long sessions with local models:

What happens now:

During a long session, the provider response ends with finish_reason: network_error (or similar)
Instead of aborting, opencode retries the entire request
The model restarts its reasoning from scratch — all thinking progress is lost
Prompt cache is preserved, so the replay is faster than a cold start, but the model still re-generates the full reasoning chain
Impact on local models (LM Studio):

Reasoning chains can take minutes; losing them on every network hiccup makes long sessions impractical
The retry is transparent (no visible error), so the user just sees the agent "thinking again" — easy to miss that progress was reset
Suggestion: consider resuming from the last stable state (e.g., keep completed tool results and only regenerate the interrupted step) instead of replaying the full turn, or make the retry budget/configurable for slow local providers.

Thanks for the note — and good questions, since this ended up getting fixed a different way than my original proposal.

On the sweep: I went with gating at the transform layer, not a client-wide grep. The merged fix (#38924, by opencode-agent) landed a version-aware regex allowlist in `transform.ts` — `GEMINI_MODELS_WITH_SAMPLING_DEFAULTS` matches only the Gemini models that still accept sampling params (2.5.x, 3-flash/pro, 3.1, 3.5-flash except -lite) and returns `undefined` for 3.5-flash-lite / 3.6. So the gating is per-model at the provider-transform layer, which is the single choke point rather than scattering guards across call sites.

On frequency: provider-side deprecations like this are rare but not exotic — in the last ~3 months I have seen Gemini dropping sampling params and a couple of Kimi/Qwen model-lineup changes (reasoning-effort variants) trigger the same class of "silently sent, then 400" failures. The general lesson I took away: blanket `id.includes("family")` matches are the hazard — version-aware matching (regex allowlist or explicit model sets) is the durable pattern.

No code changes needed from me here since #38924 covers it — but happy to help test edge cases if you hit any on your 3.x upgrade.

OpenCode Desktop backend process may not be correctly using/inheriting the Windows system proxy for the OpenAI token exchange request.
So if you use Clash or another local proxy, try setting `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, and `NO_PROXY` explicitly for OpenCode.
After adding them to Windows User Variables,  completely restarted OpenCode Desktop and the browser OAuth login worked successfully.
